newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK MCSI status seen unchanged beyond 1997 handover.
newsitem.headline: HK MCSI status seen unchanged beyond 1997 handover.

text.p: The calculator of the Morgan Stanley Capital International indices said on Thursday that Hong Kong's reversion to China next year did not by itself warrant a change in the territory's status in the indices.
Currently, Hong Kong is part of the MSCI Developed Market Indices, while China is included in the MSCI Emerging Markets Free Indices.

Geneva-based Capital International Perspective noted that the documents defining Hong Kong's status from July 1, 1997 -- the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration and the 1990 Basic Law -- enshrined provisions granting Hong Kong a high degree of autonomy except in matters of foreign affairs and defence.
There would be no exchange controls after the handover, China would not levy taxes in the territory, and the right of private ownership of property would be protected, it noted.
Rights and freedoms currently enjoyed by Hong Kong people would also be protected, it added.

Capital International said it would continue to monitor the evolution of the situation after the handover, with special attention to how the provisions are implemented, to ensure that Hong Kong's status in the MSCI Indices continued to reflect the real world opportunities available to the global investor.
